headline: Low interaction risk overall: no shared channels or write surfaces, but OCR-to-transcription chaining can still propagate errors if outputs are trusted.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: PaddleOCR can run browsers and has allowlisted egress, but Whisper has no browser, clipboard, MCP, filesystem write, or network egress. No shared communication channel is documented, so a prompt-injection bridge between the pair is not evidenced.
conditions: IF an external orchestrator copies PaddleOCR output into a prompt-bearing channel for Whisper, injection risk becomes possible.
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces.
Do not paste OCR text into instruction prompts.
Require human review before any downstream action.
Use a fixed schema for handoff data.
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to all inter-agent transfers.

B_data_leakage.rationale: PaddleOCR touches documents and images, while Whisper touches audio and speech. Neither profile shows shared filesystem access, OAuth scopes, or uncontrolled egress; Whisper is local-only by profile, so leakage across the pair is not a default pathway.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same shared folder, document or audio contents could be exposed across the workflow.
mitigations: Store inputs in separate directories.
Avoid placing sensitive files in a shared workspace.
Disable any manual export of OCR text.
Review file permissions before batch runs.
requires-engineering: add per-agent access controls.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: PaddleOCR has no documented filesystem write, git, or shell mutation surface, and Whisper explicitly cannot write files, modify git state, or spawn subprocesses. With no overlapping write authority, a capability conflict is provably blocked by the profiles.
conditions: IF an external wrapper grants both agents write access to the same mutable directory, conflict risk would need reevaluation.
mitigations: Keep outputs read-only.
Separate any generated artifacts by agent.
Do not grant shared git access.
Run each agent under distinct OS users.
requires-engineering: add locking for any shared mutable resource.

D_cascading_error.rationale: PaddleOCR produces extracted text from documents/images, and Whisper produces transcripts from audio/speech. If one agent's output is fed into the other or into a downstream action without verification, errors can cascade in default document-processing workflows even though no direct action authority is shown.
conditions: IF OCR text or transcripts are used as authoritative input to a second-stage agent without validation, downstream mistakes can propagate.
mitigations: Add a verification step before reuse.
Compare outputs against source media.
Flag low-confidence segments for review.
Keep human approval before actions.
requires-engineering: implement confidence-based gating.

E_compliance.rationale: PaddleOCR touches documents and images; Whisper touches audio and speech. No residency, certification, or retention mismatch is documented, and neither profile shows secrets or regulated-data handling. Compliance risk is therefore limited to ordinary handling gaps rather than a documented breach pathway.
conditions: IF regulated data is introduced into either pipeline, the compliance assessment must be revisited.
mitigations: Classify inputs before processing.
Avoid regulated data in test runs.
Document retention for generated artifacts.
Review vendor terms before deployment.
requires-engineering: add policy enforcement for sensitive classes.
